clue.text: Famous chapel site — sin gets reformed

indicators.note: something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sinner visits a famous chapel and comes away a better person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous chapel site' reads as one phrase, but 'site' belongs to the wordplay and the definition stops at 'chapel'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sistine Chapel in the Vatican, painted by Michelangelo, is the best-known chapel in the world.

clue.text: Distressed sort perhaps had Nikes ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters of the words before it fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is upset because their expensive trainers got wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Distressed' as dis-tressed: stripped of tresses. A shaven-headed person is one such sort, hence 'perhaps'. Nike is a sportswear brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a shaved scalp has lost their locks of hair, a punning example of someone without tresses.

clue.text: Rock makes smoother sound

parts.note: to sand wood is to rub it smooth
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Music that soothes, as if rock could make a sound gentler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music, which would pair with 'sound', but it is the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedimentary stone formed from compressed grains is a common building rock.

clue.text: Couple white magic enthrals

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the phrase before it holds the letters wanted inside itself

parts.note: the letters sitting across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A pair of lovers spellbound by benign sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people seen as a romantic pair are colloquially called an item.

clue.text: Set out from grassland in Devon river delta

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the first item goes within the second

parts.note: the Exe flows through Devon to Exeter and the sea at Exmouth
a plain is a flat grassy expanse
delta is D in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A route set out across the meadows to the mouth of a Devon river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delta' looks like part of the river scene but stands for a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out an argument is to state it clearly, which is what explained means here.

clue.text: Friendly female features in a fiction

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear inside it, so the first item sits within what follows

parts.note: a fable is an invented story
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A kindly woman appears as a character in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone friendly is good-natured and easy to talk to, which is what affable means.

clue.text: Sport among spooks upset Goldfinger?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top
something among a group sits in the middle of it, so the first item goes inside the second

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency, spooks being spies
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A James Bond villain unsettled by games played among secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldfinger's first name in the Bond novel is Auric; the question mark flags that the villain stands for his name and its sense of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric means of or relating to gold, and it is also the forename of Fleming's villain Goldfinger.

clue.text: Soft pesto put out: one's impressions?

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed and thrown into disarray, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook gives views on a sauce served too runny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressions' suggests opinions, but here it means marks pressed into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The prints a walker's feet leave in sand or mud are literally impressions made by a person.

clue.text: Curry served in bowl very cold? Not cold

indicators.note: not having something means it is left out, so the following item is dropped

parts.note: Baltic is informal British for freezing
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A diner complains that their curry arrived stone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'Baltic' means bitterly cold, after the Baltic Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spiced dish cooked and brought to the table in a small metal pan resembling a bowl.

clue.text: One leaving whole sheep's heart in dish

indicators.note: something put in another sits inside it, so the selected letter goes within the shortened word
one who is leaving departs, so that item is taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: whole means complete, all of it
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A cook removes a whole sheep's heart before serving it in a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish served at a meal can be called an entree, the course before or as the main.

clue.text: Stock retained by secret hotelier

indicators.note: something retained by another is held inside it, so the first item sits within the second

parts.note: inner feelings are private or secret
a shop that stocks goods keeps them

explanation.surface: A hotel owner quietly holds shares he tells no one about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like shares or soup, but it is the verb meaning to have in store.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs an inn or small hotel is an innkeeper, a traditional name for a hotel proprietor.

clue.text: Small bird duck left in water

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: something put in another sits inside it, so that letter goes within the word for water

parts.note: to water something is to wet it
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A little bird and a duck are left bobbing on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like another bird in the scene, but it is the cricket score of zero, shaped like O.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is called an owlet, so it is a small bird in a literal sense.

clue.text: Rinse socks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wash down with a jet of water from a pipe
second meaning: stockings and socks collectively, as in hosiery

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction for washing socks; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hose something is to spray water over it, and hose is an old word for leg coverings.

clue.text: Chipolatas then? Or bananas for local speciality?

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters before it go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Asking whether a regional dish is sausages or fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Chipolatas are small thin British sausages; 'bananas' looks like a food in the list, but it signals the reshuffle. The dish is a stew of lamb under sliced potatoes from north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This lamb and potato stew is the traditional regional dish of a county in north-west England.

clue.text: Brazil possibly tricky opposition?

parts.note: surface reading: the football team of Brazil, famously hard to beat
setter's reading: a Brazil nut has a famously hard shell, and the idiom for a difficult opponent or problem fits it literally

explanation.surface: Brazil's footballers are a hard side to play against.
explanation.walkthrough: The country's team is the decoy; the Brazil here is the hard-shelled nut, which literally is the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person or problem that is hard to overcome, and a hard-shelled Brazil nut fits the words literally.

clue.text: Spirited community? Yes and no

parts.note: surface reading: a lively, energetic neighbourhood
setter's reading: a deserted settlement is full of spirits, so it is haunted, yet has no living residents, so it is no longer a real community

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' usually means lively, but here it means inhabited by spirits; such a place is home to ghosts but not to people.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned settlement with no living inhabitants is, jokingly, home only to spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Conduct of new team Midland banker accepts

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the rearranged letters go inside the river

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; the Trent flows through the English Midlands

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the following word's letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Midlands bank takes on a new team and is judged on its behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like someone in finance; in crosswords it is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the way someone behaves towards another, so it can mean the same as conduct.

clue.text: Long time inside after arrest

indicators.note: inside means within, so the letters wanted sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: After being arrested, a prisoner serves a long stretch inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' suggests prison, which suits the arrest, but it points to letters within the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is an extended period of history, a long stretch of time.

clue.text: Unaccompanied in palace with lap dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move around and change places, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two pieces of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone alone in a palace, performing a lap dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing without instrumental accompaniment is described with this Italian musical term.

clue.text: Bird in Spooner's hut smelling bad

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the start sounds of two words change places

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut
rank means foul-smelling
say the two words with their opening sounds swapped

explanation.surface: A bird nesting in a garden hut that stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'shed rank' gives 'red shank'.
explanation.definitionFit: The redshank is a wading bird with bright red legs, common on British coasts.

clue.text: Energy in two forms for self-esteem

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
go means vigour or energy, as in full of go
instruction to read the previous word twice, giving two pieces; no letters of its own

explanation.surface: A burst of energy, in two forms, boosts one's confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two forms' tells you to use the one word twice: once as a symbol, once as a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is a person's sense of self-importance or self-worth.

clue.text: Zoom back and walk in the void

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so that word is read from right to left

parts.note: to zoom is to speed along
to pace is to walk steadily

explanation.surface: An astronaut zooms back to the craft after a walk in empty space.
explanation.definitionFit: The far reaches of the universe, beyond any planet, are the empty void of outer space.

clue.text: See 12
Destroy student no longer scholarly

parts.note: an OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
literate means learned, well-read

explanation.surface: A student drops out and is no longer an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' looks like a time phrase about the student, but it joins with 'student' to mean a past pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something out completely is to obliterate it, a strong synonym for destroy.

clue.text: Buddhist monk ensnares large creature

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap something inside, so the next item is held within the first

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist teacher
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A Tibetan monk traps a big animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal, kept for wool and as a pack beast.

clue.text: Man understood on the radio?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man's first name
second meaning: the word radio operators use to say a message was received

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like someone heard on the airwaves; the two parts are separate meanings of one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is a common male name and the radio procedure word confirming a message was received and understood.

clue.text: Work round with Manx cat?

indicators.note: a Manx cat is born without a tail, so the next word loses its final letter

parts.note: O is round in shape
puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: Someone working in a circle while a tailless cat looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx is a tailless cat breed from the Isle of Man, a crossword favourite for chopping a word's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a composition or artistic creation, as in a composer's numbered works.

clue.text: Something with bite caught enormous bird

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A huge bird is snapped up by something with sharp teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile, informally shortened, is a reptile famous for its powerful jaws.

clue.text: Scotsman in Italian river upright perhaps

indicators.note: something in another sits within it, so the name goes inside the river

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot standing upright in an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' seems to describe the Scotsman's stance, but it is a kind of instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a vertical-strung keyboard instrument, one example of the domestic piano.

clue.text: Fighter, irregular, nearly shot crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the rearranged letters go around the next item
something shot is ruined and in pieces, so the remaining letters are jumbled
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An irregular soldier, almost shot while crossing a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' looks like a description of the fighter, which suits the definition, but its letters are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is a member of a small independent armed band fighting outside a regular army.

clue.text: Sports shoe for coach

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a soft athletic shoe, the British word for a sneaker
second meaning: someone who trains athletes

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the athletic shoe Americans call a sneaker is named after training.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an athletic shoe and a person who prepares athletes, a sports coach.
